newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude weaker, further intrigue on Tapis.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude weaker, further intrigue on Tapis.

text.p: Asian crude prices weakened on Monday as talk of further Tapis deals emerged to add intrigue to the light sweet crude market.
A producer said it has sold a top-up cargo of 200,000 barrels of March Tapis at between quotes +$1.30/+$1.40, in addition to the cargo at the same level last week.
It said the two deals were not related.

Traders were searching for details to help determine the value for Tapis in March and the light sweet market because some valued it much lower. Some still said that they assessed Tapis below quotes +$1.00 per barrel.
But the producer said the relative value of Tapis versus other crudes has come in in recent weeks, making the grade more attractive, even if still negative for refinery margins.
The producer said it has now sold 1.4 million barrels of March Tapis, including an initial 600,000-barrel cargo sold "some time ago."
Traders said India awarded four Dubai cargoes for March at first-half quotes plus 43 cents to 55 cents. They said the tender results wrapped up the Dubai market for March.
However, a European major was said to still hold some ADNOC grades but it was not clear if it might keep the crude in house.

ADNOC official selling prices for January were released over the weekend and despite a slump in ADNOC premiums last month, the differentials to Dubai only came in a few cents -- surprising some players.
Swaps were quiet with brokers largely rolling over late Friday numbers. February Tapis swaps traded twice at $23.80 per barrel, sold by a European major to a trader and another European major.
